minutes.headline: Commission elects a new chair and vice chair as its longtime chair announces she is resigning
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Conservation Commission held five new wetlands hearings (73 Round Road, 52 Birch Island Way, 31 Round Road, 4 Cove Road, 215 Sunset Lane) and several continuances, approving most with standard conditions and continuing 31 Round Road, 390 Howard Street, 221 Electric Avenue and one other address to May 7. The commission discussed a legal risk in its practice of granting "default continuations" to absent applicants, addressed an unpermitted wetland-area clearing violation at 199 Massachusetts Avenue, and held officer elections: Jenny was elected chair and Rich was elected vice chair after the sitting chair announced her resignation effective end of month.

budget_items.topic: Cost of replacing a lake dock
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner said residents who leave a removable dock in over winter risk it being destroyed by ice, at which point they end up buying a replacement.

budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant's representative said the project was filed under a Category 1A single-family-lot fee, which DEP had questioned; the representative argued the fee category was correctly applied.

The chair said the office should pursue a horizontal engineering consulting RFQ, with hours still to be worked out, and that individual project reviews would otherwise be billed to applicants as budget support.

what_happened.line: The commission's longtime chair announced her resignation effective end of month, and members elected a new chair and vice chair.
The commission is reviewing legal exposure from its practice of granting default continuations to absent applicants, citing a past case where jurisdiction was lost, before issuing new guidance.

Members approved most of five new wetlands applications with standard conditions, covering a well, a septic replacement, a home addition, and driveway work, while continuing four other hearings to May 7.
Property owners at a Massachusetts Avenue address were directed to file for after-the-fact approval following unpermitted clearing in a wetland area.

why_it_matters: A change in who chairs the board that grants or conditions wetlands permits affects how future applications near Lake Shirley and Hickory Hills Lake are handled.
A shift in how the commission treats absent applicants could change permit timelines for anyone filing a wetlands application here.
The enforcement action shows that clearing work in a wetland buffer without a permit leads to a required after-the-fact filing, a process other property owners doing similar work may also face.
